config.title: FUNDA — Feature Flag Gate

intro.title: FUNDA — Feature Flag Gate
intro.body: In this lesson you will build a Feature Flag Gate — a system that fetches a remote feature-flag configuration before the Angular app boots, then makes those flags available anywhere in the app via an InjectionToken. A *featureFlag="'new-dashboard'" structural directive conditionally renders any UI block based on the flag state, and a FeatureFlagService provides programmatic access for guards and services. You will use provideAppInitializer (Angular 17+) to block app bootstrap until the remote config is loaded.
intro.usecase: Feature flags are used in virtually every production engineering team to ship code dark, run A/B tests, enable beta features per customer tier, and roll out changes incrementally without deployments.

objectives: Create an InjectionToken for the FEATURE_FLAGS config object and register it in the app providers with a useFactory
Use provideAppInitializer() (Angular 17) or APP_INITIALIZER to fetch /assets/flags.json before the app renders
Implement a FeatureFlagService that inject(FEATURE_FLAGS) and exposes isEnabled(flagKey: string): boolean
Build a *featureFlag structural directive that renders or clears its template based on FeatureFlagService.isEnabled()
Support an else template (*featureFlag="'key'; else fallback") for graceful degradation when a flag is off
Use the flag service inside a canActivate guard to block a route when a feature is disabled, redirecting to a maintenance page
Explain how this pattern differs from environment.ts and why runtime config is essential for feature flags in container-based deployments
